lessons.title: Clock Basics: Angles and Speeds
lessons.concept: An analog clock has hour and minute hands moving at constant speeds. The minute hand completes 360° in 60 minutes (6° per minute). The hour hand completes 360° in 12 hours (30° per hour or 0.5° per minute). The angle between hands can be found from their positions.
lessons.formula: Minute hand: 6° per minute. Hour hand: 0.5° per minute (or 30° per hour). Angle = |30*H - 5.5*M| degrees at H hours M minutes (smaller angle can be min(angle, 360-angle)).
lessons.worked_example: At 3:00, hour hand at 90°, minute at 0°, angle = 90°. At 3:30, hour hand at 105°, minute at 180°, angle = 75°.
mistakes: Forgetting hour hand moves as minutes pass
Using 30° per minute for hour hand instead of 0.5°
Not considering the smaller angle when asked
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Relative Speed and Coincidence/Right Angles
lessons.concept: Relative speed of minute hand with respect to hour hand is 5.5° per minute (6 - 0.5). Hands coincide when angle is 0° (every ~65 5/11 minutes in 12 hours, 11 times). They are at right angles (90°) twice in most hour intervals (22 times in 12 hours).
lessons.formula: Relative speed = 5.5°/min. Time for gain of 360° = 360/5.5 = 720/11 minutes between coincidences.
lessons.worked_example: Hands coincide at 12:00, and again after 720/11 minutes (~65 5/11 min), i.e. approximately at 1:05 5/11.
mistakes: Counting overlaps incorrectly across 12 hours (11 times, not 12)
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Calendar Basics: Odd Days and Leap Years
lessons.concept: Calendar problems use odd days (days beyond complete weeks). Ordinary year has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 odd day; leap year has 366 days = 2 odd days. Leap year rule (Gregorian): divisible by 4 is leap, except century years must be divisible by 400.
lessons.formula: Odd days: 365 mod 7 = 1, 366 mod 7 = 2. Leap year: year%400==0 or (year%4==0 and year%100!=0).
lessons.worked_example: 2000 is leap (divisible by 400). 1900 is not leap (century year not divisible by 400). 2024 is leap (divisible by 4, not century).
mistakes: Treating every year divisible by 4 as leap including centuries like 1900
Off-by-one in counting odd days across ranges
Forgetting leap day effect for dates after February

practice.question: The minute hand of a clock moves how many degrees in 1 minute?
practice.explanation: Minute hand completes 360° in 60 minutes, so 360/60 = 6° per minute.

practice.question: The hour hand moves how many degrees in 1 hour?
practice.explanation: Hour hand completes 360° in 12 hours, so 360/12 = 30° per hour.

practice.question: At 6:00, the angle between hour and minute hands is:
practice.explanation: At 6:00 hour hand points at 6 (180° from 12) and minute hand at 12 (0°), so angle is 180°.

practice.question: How many odd days are in an ordinary year (365 days)?

questions.question: How many times do clock hands coincide in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: Hands coincide once in every ~65 5/11 minutes; in 12 hours they coincide 11 times (they coincide at 12:00 but not again until after 1:00).
